transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thanks for seeing me. Well, the main reason I’m here is that anything that takes real, sitting-down brain work... I just can't seem to do it. Like doing the monthly reports for the clinics I manage, or planning a multi-site health event. It feels like I just hit an absolute wall and I keep putting it off, even when I know it really matters. 

Actually, speaking of those multi-site events, we had one last month over by the river, and the catering they ordered was from this little Italian place. Best meatballs I've had in my life. I actually tried making meatballs from scratch last weekend because of it. Bought the three-meat blend, the fresh parsley, the whole nine yards. Spent all Sunday afternoon in the kitchen. My kids wouldn't even touch them, said they looked weird. Kids are so picky these days, you know? When I was their age, we ate what was on the plate or we didn't eat. 

But... wait, what was I saying? Right, the work stuff. Yeah, the big planning tasks and reports. I just avoid them completely.
Have you noticed these kinds of attention and focus struggles since you were a kid, or is this more of a new pattern that started recently?

Oh, it’s definitely not new. It’s been like this pretty much forever. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would always tell my parents that I was a bright kid, but I was just constantly daydreaming. I was always losing my worksheets, or I'd do the homework and then just completely forget to turn it in. Honestly, the only way anything actually made it to the teacher was because my mother would physically check my backpack every single night. 

Which, actually, speaking of backpacks... my youngest son just ripped his last week. He had one of those heavy-duty canvas ones, but he completely tore the strap right off the seam because they make these kids carry so many heavy books now. I swear, his bag weighs like thirty pounds. I had to go online to order him a new one, but the shipping got delayed because of that big weather system moving through the Midwest. My sister lives out in Ohio and she said they got like eight inches of snow overnight, completely shut down her street. She had to use her neighbor's snowblower just to get her car out of the driveway... 

But, uh, anyway. No, it's not a new pattern. It's been happening since I was little.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling down or depressed. I mean, I still enjoy things, like that meatball project I mentioned. I still like watching the games on the weekends, going to my kids' soccer matches... well, most of the time. Sometimes those games drag on forever, especially when the referee calls a foul every two minutes. Last Saturday, they had this ref who must have been brand new, just blowing the whistle for every little thing. The parents on the sidelines were getting so restless. One guy actually brought a lawn chair and fell asleep right there in the middle of the first half. Woke up with a sunburn on half his face because he was facing east. Or west? Whichever way the sun was hitting him. He had to put aloe on it right there on the field... 

But yeah, no, my mood is fine. I'm just frustrated that I can't seem to get my actual work done.
Have you ever had a period of several days or more where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual without feeling tired?

No, I've never really had anything like that. I pretty much always need my sleep. If I don't get at least seven hours, I'm just dragging the next day. Like, I can't even function until I've had my coffee. I actually just bought one of those fancy espresso machines, the kind with the built-in grinder and the milk frother. I thought it would save me money instead of going to the drive-thru every morning. But honestly, figuring out the right grind size is practically a science experiment. You make it too fine, and it just drips out like molasses, and it tastes completely burnt. Too coarse, and it's just brown water. My wife was laughing at me the other morning because I went through half a bag of beans just trying to get one decent shot. The beans were from this local roaster downtown, they do these small-batch roasts... really nice people. They have a golden retriever that just hangs out in the shop, sleeping on the floor. 

But, uh, anyway. No, no periods of crazy energy or not sleeping. Just my normal, tired self.
Would you say these attention and focus difficulties cause real problems for you in more than one area of your life, like both at work and at home?

Yeah, it definitely spills over into pretty much everything. I mean, I'm still getting by at work, managing the clinic, and I'm still involved in the community, but... it's getting harder. Like, my staff has had to cover gaps for me more times than I want to admit, and I've let some important deadlines slip. I've had to make so many embarrassing, last-minute apologies to coworkers and even to my friends. 

Speaking of apologies, I had to send this huge fruit basket to our clinic's IT guy last month because I completely forgot to submit the software renewal forms he needed. He was so stressed out about it. Those fruit baskets are getting so expensive, though. I ordered it from that place that cuts the pineapples into little daisy shapes? My wife loves those. We got one for her mother's birthday last year, but the delivery driver left it on the porch in the middle of July, and by the time she got home from her bridge club, the chocolate-covered strawberries had completely melted into this huge, sticky puddle. The ants found it, too. Have you ever tried to get sugar ants off a concrete porch? It's impossible. We had to use the power washer, which I hadn't started in like three years, so of course the carburetor was gunked up...

But, um, yeah. To answer your question, yes. It causes problems at work, at home, with friends... pretty much everywhere.
Do you often feel physically restless, fidgety, or find yourself interrupting others or blurting things out before they finish talking?

No, not really. I mean, I'm not bouncing off the walls or anything. I don't really interrupt people either. Well, my wife might say I do sometimes, but that's usually just when we're watching Jeopardy and I know the answer before she does. I'm actually pretty good at trivia, especially geography. I almost went on a game show once in college, but my car broke down on the way to the audition. It was this old Honda Civic, rust on the wheel wells, you know the type. The alternator just gave out right on the highway. I had to wait two hours for a tow truck, and the driver was this guy who wouldn't stop talking about his conspiracy theories regarding the moon landing. He had all these diagrams in the cab of the truck. Said the lighting was all wrong in the photos. I didn't really know what to say, so I just nodded along until we got to the garage. The mechanic there was great, though, fixed it up for like eighty bucks... 

But no, I don't feel physically restless or blurt things out. I'm pretty calm physically, it's just my brain that won't stay on track.
